intervention_or_language: Screen-reader-native semantic HTML/MathML; EPUB; tagged PDF; audio/DAISY
measure_definition: Blindness under vision-impairment definitions cited by the GBD study.
source_title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of childhood visual impairment
applicable_interventions: screen-reader-native semantic HTML; MathML; EPUB; tagged PDF; audio/DAISY
double_count_rule: Subset/overlap of broader visual impairment and assistive-technology populations; never sum.
limitations: Blindness does not imply screen-reader use; access mode varies by person, task, literacy, device, and context.

intervention_or_language: Screen-reader-native semantic HTML/MathML; EPUB; tagged PDF; audio/DAISY
measure_definition: People with near or distance vision impairment.
source_locator: Key facts and prevalence: at least 2.2 billion
applicable_interventions: semantic HTML; MathML; EPUB; tagged PDF; audio/DAISY; scalable text
double_count_rule: Includes many people who do not need a screen reader and overlaps blindness, literacy, dementia, and AT need; never sum.
limitations: Heterogeneous severity and correction status; no digital access-mode measure.

measure_label: Needs one or more assistive products
population_universe: Children and adults with disabilities and older persons globally
measure_definition: Need for one or more assistive products across mobility, hearing, self-care, vision, cognition, and communication.
source_title: Global Report on Assistive Technology launch
source_locator: More than 2.5 billion need one or more assistive products
applicable_interventions: screen readers; communication/cognition apps; accessible digital and physical formats
double_count_rule: Umbrella population overlaps every disability-access intervention and cannot be allocated or added across formats.
limitations: Not specific to reading, education, digital content, or any one assistive product.

measure_label: People needing assistive technology who are denied access
population_universe: People in the global assistive-technology need population
measure_definition: People needing one or more assistive products who lack access.
source_title: Global Report on Assistive Technology launch
source_locator: Nearly one billion denied access; access in some LMICs as low as 3%
applicable_interventions: screen readers; communication/cognition apps; accessible digital and physical formats
double_count_rule: Nested within the more-than-2.5-billion need population; do not add to it.
limitations: Not specific to educational content or any single accessibility format.

measure_label: Websites failing WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships
measure_definition: Percentage of tested websites with WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships issues.
source_title: Accessibility monitoring of public sector websites and mobile apps from 2022 to 2024
applicable_interventions: semantic HTML; labeled structures; native tables/headings/forms; MathML for mathematical content
double_count_rule: Website failure rate cannot be combined with person counts or treated as the MathML failure rate.
limitations: Public-sector UK sample; simplified testing covers limited pages and criteria; MathML was not separately measured.

measure_label: Sites where PDF errors were the largest error category
measure_definition: PDF errors accounted for the highest total number of errors on the site.
source_title: Ireland's Monitoring Report for the EU Web Accessibility Directive 2023
source_locator: Executive summary, PDF p. 6: 137 of 231 sites; p. 7 recommends HTML instead of PDF forms
applicable_interventions: tagged PDF; semantic HTML alternative; accessible forms
double_count_rule: Site count is not a count of PDFs or people and cannot be combined with user-population overlays.
limitations: Indicates error dominance, not that every PDF on each site failed; tagging alone does not guarantee cognitive or visual usability.

intervention_or_language: Accessible EPUB and other born-accessible publications
reference_year: current portal; estimate date not stated
measure_label: Published materials readable by blind or low-vision people
population_universe: All published materials in the World Blind Union estimate
measure_definition: Share estimated readable by blind or low-vision people.
source_locator: WBU estimates less than 10% of all published materials can be read by blind or low-vision people
applicable_interventions: accessible EPUB; DAISY; braille; audio; born-accessible publishing
double_count_rule: Do not convert a materials share into people or add it to population counts.
limitations: Estimate date, publication universe, and sampling method are not stated on the portal; not EPUB-specific.

population_universe: National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled readership
measure_definition: Readers served using audio; NLS digital talking-book players support DAISY/ANSI-NISO formats.
source_title: Annual Report of the Librarian of Congress, FY2024
applicable_interventions: audio; DAISY digital talking books; navigable offline cartridges
double_count_rule: Do not add audio, BARD, cartridge, and braille readership categories; they overlap.
limitations: One national service system; excludes eligible nonusers and other audio-book services; annual report notes one library data issue in the overall total.

measure_definition: Adults lacking basic literacy skills under UIS reporting.
source_locator: Key facts: 739 million adults age 15+ lack basic literacy skills
applicable_interventions: plain language; easy-read; audio; pictorial support; assisted completion
double_count_rule: May overlap low measured literacy, dementia, disability, language mismatch, and offline populations; never sum.
limitations: Lack of basic literacy is not synonymous with cognitive disability or a preference for one plain-language standard.

measure_label: Adults at literacy Level 1 or below
population_universe: Adults age 16-65 in participating OECD countries
measure_definition: Average share scoring at Level 1 or below on the PIAAC literacy scale.
source_title: Adult literacy skills / Survey of Adult Skills 2023
source_locator: PIAAC Cycle 2: 26% of adults at Level 1 or below; 31 countries participated in Round 1
applicable_interventions: plain language; clear structure; worked examples; assisted completion
double_count_rule: Do not apply the 26% average to nonparticipants or add it to UNESCO's global count.
limitations: Cross-country average, not a global rate; country rates vary substantially.

applicable_interventions: plain language; easy-read; consistent navigation; audio; supported decision-making
double_count_rule: Overlaps literacy, visual, AT, ageing, and connectivity populations; never sum.
limitations: Dementia is heterogeneous; accessibility needs vary by stage, person, and task.

intervention_or_language: Low-bandwidth/offline bundles and print-ready service routes
measure_definition: People not using the Internet under ITU usage concepts.
source_locator: Six billion online; 2.2 billion remain offline
applicable_interventions: low-bandwidth bundles; offline packages; downloadable media; print-ready forms; phone and face-to-face routes
double_count_rule: Overlaps youth without home internet, remote-learning exclusion, disability, literacy, and language groups; use once as broad context.
limitations: Internet nonuse is not the same as inability to use any digital delivery; no educational-resource-specific measure.

measure_label: Children and young people without internet at home
population_universe: Children and young people age 25 or less
source_title: How many children and young people have internet access at home?
source_locator: Key messages: 2.2 billion age 25 or less; more than 65%
applicable_interventions: offline learning bundles; downloadable packages; broadcast; print
double_count_rule: Do not add school-age 1.3 billion and youth 760 million subgroups; ages 15-17 overlap and both sit within the age-0-25 total.
limitations: Home internet differs from any internet use; source surveys span 2010-2020; pandemic-era snapshot.

population_universe: Students from pre-primary through upper-secondary affected by school closures

applicable_interventions: offline bundles; radio; television; print take-home materials

intervention_or_language: Print-ready forms and supported offline routes
measure_label: Digital should never be the only option
population_universe: People who prefer or need offline access to public services
measure_definition: Public services should provide supported offline routes including phone lines, paper forms, and face-to-face support where appropriate.
source_title: Digital Inclusion Action Plan: One Year On progress report, large print
source_locator: PDF p. 28: digital should never be the only option
applicable_interventions: print-ready forms; phone; face-to-face; large print; braille; audio
double_count_rule: Reuse independently measured offline/print-disability overlays; do not invent a separate paper-form population.
limitations: UK service policy, not a global prevalence estimate; ordinary print is not automatically accessible.
